title: Customer Safelist and Staged Exposure for Model Catalog Onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Define a lightweight, repeatable pathway for enterprise customer requests to onboard new model variants or request version pinning without risking production regressions for other customers. Background: Customers increasingly request pinned versions, bespoke quantized variants, or expedited onboarding for compliance reasons. Current intake funnels and eval gates are optimized for catalog-level releases but lack a formal path for sponsor-backed, limited-exposure rollouts and safe deprecation cadence. Proposal summary: Create a 'safelist + staged exposure' workflow where an approved customer (sponsor) can request a model variant be safelisted for controlled exposure. Steps include: 1) Intake scorer assigns initial lane (safelist vs public) using risk signals and SLA requirements. 2) Automated lightweight evals run on sponsor-supplied prompt sets and standard regressions. 3) If evals pass, start a shadow trial (non-traffic) window with telemetry hooks; then a sponsor-led canary with pinned routing for a fixed percentage of the sponsor's traffic. 4) Define metrics thresholds for stability (latency, error rate, quality regressions) and an automatic rollback / pin-expiry mechanism. 5) Standardize an audit trail, KMS key usage, and required security checklist for private deployments. Why this is different: instead of full public catalog promotion, this creates a controlled lane where enterprise customers can get faster access while preserving platform-wide SLOs and enabling reversible, observable rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form updated to collect sponsor, customer prompt set link, compliance constraints, and preferred pin duration
Automation: eval pipeline can run sponsor prompt set + standard regressions and produce pass/fail summary
Shadow mode implemented: model can be deployed to shadow for a customer without affecting live routing
Canary/pinned routing: per-customer pin of a model variant up to configured percentage with time-limited expiry
Telemetry gates: predefined thresholds for latency, error rate, and quality delta that trigger automatic rollback
Audit: launch records include sponsor approval, eval artifacts link, and timestamped decision log
success_metrics: Median time from request to limited-customer rollout reduced to <= 7 days
No more than 1 regressions-caused incident per 100 safelist rollouts in first 90 days
80% of enterprise pin requests complete shadow + canary without manual rollback
CSAT for sponsored onboarding >= 4.0 (5-point scale) following rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Intake): Update product intake form and scoring rules; sample rollout with two strategic customers
Phase 1 (Eval Automation): Ship lightweight eval runner integration and report format (internal only)
Phase 2 (Shadow Mode): Enable per-customer shadow deployments and capture KV/latency/quality telemetry
Phase 3 (Sponsor Canary): Implement pinned routing and time-limited pin expiry with auto-unpin
Phase 4 (Ops Runbook): Publish runbook for support, rollback, and deprecation notices
Phase 5 (Policy): Codify deprecation windows and communication templates for customers and internal stakeholders
tradeoffs: Faster sponsored access increases engineering surface area for per-customer routing and telemetry; adds ongoing maintenance cost
Shadow and canary lanes may delay full catalog promotion because stability signal requirements become stricter
Automated evals reduce manual review but may miss domain-specific failure modes unless sponsor prompt sets are comprehensive
open_questions: What is the minimum set of telemetry signals required to consider a canary healthy for enterprise SLAs?
How long should default pin durations be (30 / 90 / 180 days) and what is the auto-renewal policy?
Do we require legal/sponsor SLA signature for any pin > 90 days?
Should we provision separate audit retention for safelist events under enterprise compliance requests?
